S40.01.needs: a signed-in AGI account in Cloud mode
S40.01.note: The CLI only saves the value; that replies use it is applied on the server and cannot be checked from CLI code.
steps: Check that the chat is signed in and in Cloud mode; if it is not, type /model and switch to Cloud mode.
Type /personalize set name Sam (any name up to 60 characters).
Type /personalize show and check that the line labelled What to call you shows the name.
Ask a question and check whether the reply uses that name, then compare with Expected.
S40.01.where: Type /personalize set name <value> in the chat, then /personalize show

S40.02.needs: a signed-in AGI account in Cloud mode
steps: Check that the chat is signed in and in Cloud mode.
Type /personalize set about I run a small bakery that sells online. (up to 1500 characters).
Type /personalize show and check that the line labelled About you shows the text.
Ask a question that depends on the background, such as what to name a new product, and compare the reply with Expected.
S40.02.where: Type /personalize set about <text> in the chat, then /personalize show

S40.03.needs: a signed-in AGI account in Cloud mode
S40.03.note: Tailoring of the reply happens on the server, not in CLI code.
steps: Check that the chat is signed in and in Cloud mode.
Type /personalize set work high school chemistry teacher (up to 120 characters).
Type /personalize show and check that the line labelled Your work or role shows the text.
Ask for help with a task from that job and check whether the reply is tailored to it.
S40.03.where: Type /personalize set work <text> in the chat, then /personalize show

S40.05.note: This is the CLI output style, separate from the account Response style in S40.07.
steps: Type /output-style and read the Available styles: list; the active one has a * beside it.
Type /output-style concise.
Ask a question such as How do I reverse a list in Python? and check the reply follows the chosen style.
Type /output-style again and check the active style is the one you picked.
S40.05.where: Type /output-style in the chat to list the styles, then /output-style <name> to pick one

S40.07.needs: a signed-in AGI account in Cloud mode
S40.07.note: formal is one value of the Response style field, the only formality setting found in the code, and it applies to Cloud turns.
steps: Check that the chat is signed in and in Cloud mode.
Type /personalize set style formal.
Type /personalize show and check that the line labelled Response style shows formal.
Ask a question and check whether the reply uses a more formal register, then compare with Expected.
S40.07.where: Type /personalize set style formal in the chat, then /personalize show

S40.08.note: The named presets are the output styles; no separate tone-preset list was found.
steps: Type /output-style and read the list: default, proactive, concise, explanatory, learning and study.
Type /output-style study.
Ask a question and check that one preset governs the reply.
Type /output-style default to go back, and compare with Expected.

S40.09.needs: a signed-in AGI account in Cloud mode
S40.09.note: The tone change is applied on the server, not in CLI code.
steps: Check that the chat is signed in and in Cloud mode.
Type /personalize set warmth more.
Type /personalize show and check that the line labelled Warmth shows more.
Ask a question and check whether the reply is warmer; then type /personalize set warmth less and ask again to compare.
S40.09.where: Type /personalize set warmth more in the chat, then /personalize show

S40.10.needs: a signed-in AGI account in Cloud mode
S40.10.note: The reply change is applied on the server, not in CLI code.
steps: Check that the chat is signed in and in Cloud mode.
Type /personalize set enthusiasm less.
Type /personalize show and check that the line labelled Enthusiasm shows less.
Ask a question and check whether the reply is less enthusiastic, then compare with Expected.
S40.10.where: Type /personalize set enthusiasm less in the chat, then /personalize show

S40.11.needs: a signed-in AGI account in Cloud mode
S40.11.note: Two fields cover this: the Formatting choice and the Headings and lists slider.
steps: Check that the chat is signed in and in Cloud mode.
Type /personalize set formatting prose.
Type /personalize show and check that the line labelled Formatting shows prose.
Ask a question that has several parts and check whether the reply uses prose instead of headings and lists, then compare with Expected.
S40.11.where: Type /personalize set headings less in the chat, or /personalize set formatting prose, then /personalize show

S40.12.needs: a signed-in AGI account in Cloud mode
S40.12.note: The reply change is applied on the server, not in CLI code.
steps: Check that the chat is signed in and in Cloud mode.
Type /personalize set emoji less.
Type /personalize show and check that the line labelled Emoji shows less.
Ask a question and check whether the reply has fewer or no emoji, then compare with Expected.
S40.12.where: Type /personalize set emoji less in the chat, then /personalize show

S40.13.needs: a signed-in AGI account in Cloud mode
steps: Check that the chat is signed in and in Cloud mode.
Type /personalize set technical beginner.
Type /personalize show and check that the line labelled Technical level shows beginner.
Ask a technical question and check whether the reply is simpler, then compare with Expected.
S40.13.where: Type /personalize set technical beginner in the chat, then /personalize show

S40.14.needs: a signed-in AGI account in Cloud mode
steps: Check that the chat is signed in and in Cloud mode.
Type /personalize set language fr.
Type /personalize show and check that the line labelled Reply language shows fr.
Ask a question in English and check whether the reply is written in French, then compare with Expected.
Type /personalize set language auto to go back.
S40.14.where: Type /personalize set language fr in the chat, then /personalize show

S40.16.needs: none for the file instructions; a signed-in account for the web custom instructions
S40.16.note: No on/off switch for memory instruction files was found in the code; the web custom-instructions page is outside apps/cli, so its toggle is unverified.
steps: Type /memory add global Always answer in short bullet points.
Type /memory and check that the [global] entry under Memory Hierarchy: is found and shows a preview of the text.
Start a new chat, ask a question, and check the reply follows the instruction.
Look for a control that switches the instruction off without deleting it; none was found in the CLI, so compare with Expected and note the result.
S40.16.where: Type /memory add global <text> in the chat; standing account custom instructions are set on the web under Settings > General, which /personalize show prints as a link

S40.17.needs: a project folder with a git repository or project file
S40.17.note: Project instructions are the CLAUDE.md file at the project root; in the full-screen view /memory edit is refused, so use /memory add.
steps: Open a terminal in the project folder and start agi there.
Type /memory add project Use metric units.
Type /memory and check that the [project] entry is found with its path.
Start a new chat in the same folder, ask a question that involves units, and check the reply follows the instruction.
S40.17.where: In the project folder, type /memory add project <text> in the chat

S40.18.note: The quick-apply step /agents <name> was verified in the full-screen UI code only.
steps: Type /agents create reviewer (add --global for all projects).
Type /agents path reviewer and open the file it names in a text editor.
Write the instructions in the body of the file below the header lines, and save.
Type /agents show reviewer and check the prompt body shows your instructions.
Type /agents reviewer to apply it to this session, ask a question, and compare with Expected.
S40.18.where: Type /agents create <name> in the chat, then /agents path <name> to find the file to write the instructions in

labels.text: for this session only; your saved default is unchanged.

steps: Type /output-style and note the active style and the saved default.
Type /output-style learning --session.
Ask a question and check the reply follows the session-only style.
Start a new chat or type /output-style and check the saved default has not changed.

S40.23.note: No single action that resets all style preferences was found; the nearest are /output-style default (back to the built-in default style) and /personalize clear <field> for one field at a time. Searched apps/cli for reset and clear actions.

labels.text: Educational. Adds insight blocks explaining each non-trivial choice.

steps: Type /output-style explanatory.
Ask a question such as Why does Python use indentation?
Check the reply explains its reasoning and adds insight blocks, then compare with Expected.

labels.text: Interactive. Completes changes and adds one optional learning exercise.
Teaches step by step with questions instead of finished answers.

S40.25.note: The learning style's own description is one optional exercise, not quizzing; the study style matches the step-by-step teaching in Expected more closely.
steps: Type /output-style learning.
Ask a question about a coding task and check the reply adds one optional learning exercise.
Type /output-style study and ask the same question to compare the step-by-step teaching style.
Compare what you see with Expected.

labels.text: Leads with the result; no preamble, narration or recap.

steps: Type /output-style concise.
Ask a question that could have a long answer, such as How do I install git on a Mac?
Check the reply leads with the result with no preamble or recap, then compare with Expected.

S40.27.note: Delete removes the style file directly in the code with no Trash step, and editing is done in the file itself, not in the chat.
steps: Type /output-style new brief-notes Keep every answer under three sentences.
Type /output-style and check brief-notes is listed; the creation message gives the file path to edit.
Type /output-style brief-notes, ask a question, and check the reply follows it.
Type /output-style delete brief-notes and check the message says Deleted output style brief-notes.

S40.28.note: In the full-screen view /output-style only shows the Active list and not the In effect block; that block comes from the plain REPL path.
steps: Type /output-style with no name.
Check the In effect for this session: block shows the output style and where it comes from, and the Instructions lines list the memory files found.
Type /memory and check the Memory Hierarchy: list shows which instruction files are found.
Compare with Expected.
S40.28.where: Type /output-style in the chat (no name), then /memory

labels.text: Migrate settings from another coding CLI. Defaults to Claude Code.

S40.29.needs: Claude Code settings on this Mac
S40.29.note: The in-chat /import and /migrate commands move old conversation history, not preferences.
steps: In a terminal (not in the chat), type agi migrate --dry-run.
Read the Claude Code migration dry run report, including the Source line and the MCP line.
Type agi migrate to import for real.
Check the report says Claude Code migration complete and that the imported items appear.
S40.29.where: In a terminal outside the chat, run agi migrate --dry-run, then agi migrate
